ja: אלי אלדעה, לם יסתפזה אלהוי ולא אנכ'דע בסחר אלדניא, סקטהֵ ענה מאונהֵ אלתערץ' ואלתסבב לאסתג'לאב רזקה לסקוט אלוג'הין אלמד'כורין ענה, אעני אלאכ'תבאר ואלבטר באלנעמה, ואתאה רזקה בגיר משקה ולא כלפה חסב אלבלגה ואלקות, כמא קאל לא ירעיב ה' נפש צדיק. פאן קאל קאיל אנא קד נשאהד בעץ' אלצאלחין לא תתהיא להם ארזאקהם אלא בעד אלכלפה ואלמשקה, וכת'יר מן אהל אלעציאן קד תודעוא ועישהם ארגד עיש ואהנאה. קלת, קד תקדם ללאנביא ואלאפאצ'ל אלבחת' ען הד'א אלמעני, פמנהם מן קאל מדוע דרך רשעים צלחה, וקאל אכ'ר למה תראיני און ועמל תביט ושוד וחמס לנגדי ויהי ריב ומדון ישא, וקאל כי רשע מכתיר את הצדיק, וקאל תחריש כבלע רשע צדיק ממנו, וקאל אכ'ר הנה אלה רשעים ושלוי עולם השגו חיל, וקאל אך ריק זכיתי לבבי וארחץ בנקיון כפי ואהי נגוע כל היום ותוכחתי לבקרים, וקאל אכ'ר עלי לסאן אהל עצרה גם נבנו עושי רשעה גם בחנו אלהים וימלטו, וכת'יר מת'ל ד'לך. לכן אכ'תצר אלנבי אלג'ואב ען שרח עלהֵ ד'לך, לאן עלהֵ כל ואחד מן אלצאלחין אלממתחנין וכל ואחד מן אלטאלחין אלמנעמין פי הד'ה אלדאר גיר עלהֵ אלאכ'ר, לכנה נבה עלי ד'לך בקולה הנסתרות לה' אלהינו והנגלות לנו ולבנינו. וקאל אלחכים פי מת'ל ד'לך אם עשק רש וגזל משפט וצדק תראה במדינה אל תתמה על החפץ, וקאל אלכתאב הצור תמים פעלו כי כל דרכיו משפט. ומע ד'לך ארי אן אבין פי ד'לך מא יכון פיה בעץ' אלאקנאע, ואקול, אן אלוג'ה אלד'י מן אג'לה יתעד'ר עלי אלפאצ'ל מג'י רזקה חתי

The second aspect: that if the human were spared the toil and engagement and causing in attracting his sustenance, he would exult and grow insolent, and hasten to acts of disobedience, and pay no regard to the dues of the blessings of God upon him — as He said: "And there shall be lyre and lute, drum and pipe, and wine at their banquets — but the work of the Lord they regard not, and the deed of His hands they do not see" (Isaiah 5:12); and He said: "And Jeshurun grew fat and kicked; you grew fat, gross, gorged, and he forsook the God who made him" (Deuteronomy 32:15). The early ones said: "Beautiful is the study of the Law together with worldly occupation, for the labor of both makes sin be forgotten; and any Torah without occupation alongside it — its end is annulment, and it draws sin in its wake" (m. Avot 2:2); and more rightful is the one deprived of both, his mind preoccupied with neither.

So it was of the gentleness of the Creator (exalted be He) toward the human that He preoccupied him with the affairs of his this-world and his next-world, that he might be occupied throughout the span of his life with that — and not seek what does not concern him and what his intellect cannot grasp, such as the matters of beginning and end, as He said: "He has even put the world into their heart, without which the human cannot find out the work that God has done from beginning to end" (Ecclesiastes 3:11). If, then, he is one who prefers obedience to God, who chooses His worship, who relies upon Him in the affairs of his religion and his worldly life — withdrawing from vile traits, longing for excellences, neither exulting in ease nor at home in slackness, neither seized by appetite nor deceived by the world's enchantment — the burden of engagement and causing for the attraction of his sustenance falls away from him, on account of the falling away from him of the two aspects mentioned, namely, the testing and the insolent boasting in the blessing. His sustenance comes to him without weariness or burden, in proportion to need and subsistence, as He said: "The Lord shall not let the soul of the righteous starve" (Proverbs 10:3).

If a speaker should say: "We see some of the righteous whose sustenance is not made ready for them except after burden and weariness; and many of the people of disobedience are at ease, and their living is the most prosperous and pleasant" — I say: this concept has already been investigated by the prophets and the excellent ones. Among them is one who said: "Why does the way of the wicked prosper?" (Jeremiah 12:1); and another said: "Why do You make me see iniquity, and look upon trouble — destruction and violence are before me; there is contention, and strife arises" (Habakkuk 1:3); and he said: "When the wicked surrounds the righteous" (Habakkuk 1:4); and: "Why do You keep silent when the wicked swallows the righteous more righteous than he?" (Habakkuk 1:13). Another said: "Behold, these are the wicked, and ever at ease they have grown rich" (Psalms 73:12); and: "Surely in vain have I purified my heart and washed my hands in innocence; for I have been afflicted all the day, and my chastisement comes in the mornings" (Psalms 73:13–14). Another said, on the tongue of the people of his time: "They have built up the doers of wickedness; they have even tested God and escaped" (Malachi 3:15) — and many like that.
